question: What is the main goal of doing a situation analysis in community health nursing?

options.A: To gather comprehensive data about population health and resources
options.B: To punish local leaders for failing to meet health targets
options.C: To replace traditional healers with western medical doctors
options.D: To enforce strict government regulations on local businesses

explanation: Spot on! Before planning any care, you need to understand the community's actual health status and available resources so your efforts hit the mark. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T7#GNS124_U3_T7_h1)

question: Why shouldn't you rely purely on assumptions when planning a new community health program?

options.A: Assumptions automatically increase the spread of infectious diseases
options.B: Assumptions are illegal to use in official government health reports
options.C: Assumptions take more time to calculate than actual field surveys
options.D: Assumptions often lead to programs addressing problems the community does not prioritize

explanation: Exactly! If you plan based on guesses instead of facts, you might end up solving problems the locals don't even care about, leading to wasted effort. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T7#GNS124_U3_T7_h1)

question: Which of these is the best example of a quantitative data collection tool?

options.B: General observations of community dance festivals
options.D: Unstructured daily field notes from village elders

explanation: You got it! Quantitative data is all about numbers and measurable facts, which structured questionnaires give you. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T7#GNS124_U3_T7_h2)

question: You need to find out the exact rate of childhood malnutrition in a rural ward. Where should you check first?

options.A: Local clinic weighing registers and child welfare records
options.B: Folktales told by elderly residents around the evening fire
options.C: Abstract political essays written by national lawmakers
options.D: General gossip gathered at the community market square

explanation: Spot on! Clinic records give you the actual numbers and history on child growth and facility use. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T7#GNS124_U3_T7_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of using qualitative tools in a community assessment?

options.A: To capture local attitudes, cultural beliefs, and human stories
options.B: To measure precise blood pressure and body temperature
options.C: To calculate exact mathematical disease prevalence rates
options.D: To count the total number of hospital beds in the district

explanation: Brilliant! Qualitative methods help you understand the 'why' behind people's behaviors rather than just raw numbers. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T7#GNS124_U3_T7_h3)

question: Why would you want to conduct a key informant interview with a respected local elder?

options.A: To test the reading and writing skills of the village leadership
options.B: To force the elder to pay for community health insurance schemes
options.C: To gain deep, expert insights into the community's history and health barriers
options.D: To replace the need for any quantitative surveys in the village

explanation: Correct! Key informants hold valuable local knowledge that helps explain why certain health habits stick around. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T7#GNS124_U3_T7_h3)

question: What makes Participatory Rural Appraisal (PRA) different from traditional surveys?

options.A: It focuses only on collecting numerical laboratory test results
options.B: It is conducted entirely by foreign experts without local input
options.C: It requires expensive computers and satellite internet connections
options.D: It actively involves community members in analyzing their own conditions

explanation: Well done! PRA puts the community in the driver's seat to evaluate their own challenges. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T7#GNS124_U3_T7_h4)

question: You want to find out which months malaria cases peak and food is scarcest in a farming village. Which tool should you use?
explanation: Spot on! Seasonal calendars let you visually map out changes across the year, tracking things like disease cycles and food supply. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T7#GNS124_U3_T7_h4)

question: What is a transect walk during an environmental scan?

options.A: A systematic walk through the community to observe conditions firsthand
options.B: A physical exercise routine taught to pregnant women at the clinic
options.C: A laboratory test used to measure water contamination levels
options.D: A legal court session held to resolve community land disputes

explanation: Correct! A transect walk means walking a set path through the community to see housing, sanitation, and hazards with your own eyes. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T7#GNS124_U3_T7_h5)

question: Why is drawing a community map so useful for health planning?

options.A: It guarantees financial grants from international donor agencies
options.B: It provides exact genetic profiles of every newborn in the ward
options.C: It replaces the need for nurses to ever visit the village physically
options.D: It reveals geographical inequalities and the physical location of health hazards

explanation: Brilliant! Mapping shows you where resources and environmental dangers are located, helping you reach isolated spots. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T7#GNS124_U3_T7_h5)

question: What does data triangulation mean in community health assessment?

options.A: Interviewing exactly three family members per household
options.B: Comparing information from multiple sources to check for consistency
options.C: Dividing a survey questionnaire into three equal sections
options.D: Using three different brands of weighing scales for accuracy

explanation: You got it! Triangulation is simply cross-checking your survey results, interviews, and records to make sure your findings are solid. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T7#GNS124_U3_T7_h6)

question: Villagers complain of no clean water during interviews, but clinic records show zero water-borne diseases. What is your best next step?

options.A: Investigate further using triangulation to uncover the true water situation
options.B: Close down the local health clinic immediately for poor record-keeping
options.C: Dismiss the villagers' complaints because clinic records are always right
options.D: Punish the health records officer for falsifying government documents

explanation: Spot on! When sources don't match up, don't just ignore one—dig deeper and cross-check to find the real picture. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T7#GNS124_U3_T7_h6)
